candidates.title: Kingman, Arizona saucer crash and Arthur Stansel's impact-velocity assignment
candidates.quote: They were told a secret test vehicle had crashed. His job was to determine its impact velocity.

link.reason: Both tell Arthur Stansel's account of the 1953 Kingman crash, where he was sent in to work out the crash's ballistics.
link.difference: Describes his task as finding the impact velocity of what he was told was a secret test vehicle. It leaves out the small being in the tent and credits Chris Mellon.

candidates.title: Stansel: told it was a classified US government vehicle
candidates.quote: I accepted it was probably some United States government uh vehicle, a highly classified vehicle. In fact, we were told that that's what it was.

link.reason: This is Stansel telling, first hand, the same Kingman account as telling 1, where crew were told a secret test vehicle had crashed.
link.difference: Stansel himself says he accepted it was a highly classified US government vehicle because that is what they were told.

candidates.title: Declassified Upshot-Knothole report puts Stansel at the Nevada tests
candidates.quote: And a declassified report from Operation Upshot Knol confirms Stansel was on site for the nuclear testing there.

link.reason: This telling is about a declassified report placing Stansel at the Nevada nuclear tests. The nearest story is a theory that the Upshot-Knothole tests disturbed the craft, which is a different claim.

candidates.title: Dr. Eric Wang's Department of Special Studies moves to Sandia
candidates.place_text: Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio; Sandia/Kirtland AFB, New Mexico

documents: Obituary of Eric H. Wang in a mechanical engineering magazine

link.reason: Both tell of Eric Wang's special projects department at Wright-Patterson, and the story already places it at Kirtland too.
link.difference: Adds that the department moved to Sandia/Kirtland in 1956 and cites Wang's obituary and William Steinman.

candidates.title: Maria Wang says her husband reported directly to Henry Kissinger
candidates.quote: She said that her husband had reported directly to Henry Kissinger.

link.reason: Maria Wang's claim that her husband reported to Kissinger is one point inside the story about Steinman's book on the Aztec crash, so it is narrower than that story.

candidates.title: Kissinger among the first CIC officers in Oberammergau
candidates.quote: Henry Kissinger was one of the first officers to occupy the barracks there in 1945.

link.reason: Kissinger moving into the Oberammergau barracks in 1945 is one specific event. The nearest story makes a general claim about his counterintelligence tech-retrieval role.

candidates.title: CIC interrogates Viktor Schauberger for nine months
candidates.quote: According to historian Nick Cook's great book, The Hunt for Zero Point, CIC agents interrogated Shaburgger for nine months, fully aware of his most classified work.

link.reason: The nine-month CIC interrogation of Schauberger is a separate event from the stories about him being tricked into signing over his work.

candidates.title: CIC agent tricks Schauberger into signing his work over; IP ends up at Brookhaven
candidates.place_text: Europe; Brookhaven National Lab, Long Island
candidates.quote: After the war ended, another Army CIC agent, Neil Gershimer, tricked Shawberger into signing all of his work over to the United States.

link.reason: Both tell of the Army CIC tricking Schauberger into handing over his propulsion work, which then ended up at Brookhaven.

downgraded.why: a reverse-engineering telling and the program story schauberger-s-propulsion-work-taken-to-brookhaven: a program and a story of another kind are different grains

candidates.quote: suddenly becomes the director of Harvard Observatory and he destroys onethird of the photographic place

link.reason: Both tell of Menzel destroying Harvard photographic plates, documented by Dorrit Hoffleit (spelled here as 'Dory Toughlight').
link.difference: Told by Villarroel, who says a third of the plates were destroyed after he became observatory director.

candidates.title: Menzel named in the MJ12 documents
candidates.quote: Adding to the mystery, Menzel was named in the MJ12 documents as part of Truman's top secret UFO research panel in the late 1940s.

link.reason: Both tell of Menzel's name appearing in the MJ12 documents.
link.difference: Places it in the late 1940s on Truman's top secret UFO panel and is told by the host rather than Villarroel.

candidates.title: Branscomb allegedly offers Condon his clearance back for burying the UFO question
candidates.quote: As director of the National Bureau of Standards, Bransome allegedly offered committee chair Edward Condan a deal. Help bury the UFO question and get your security clearance back.

link.reason: Both tell of Lewis Branscomb offering Edward Condon his security clearance back, tied to Condon heading the UFO study.

candidates.title: Kissinger consults for the Psychological Strategy Board
candidates.quote: In 1951, 1952, and again in [music] 1955, he worked as a consultant for the Psychological Strategy Board and its [music] successor, the Operations Coordinating Board.

link.reason: Kissinger working as a consultant to the Psychological Strategy Board is a different story from the PSB being the source of alien lore and from his Army counterintelligence work.

candidates.title: Corso's claim of reverse-engineered alien tech
candidates.quote: Corso went on to claim in his book, The Day After Roswell, that alien tech had been recovered and reverse engineered from crash retrieval programs.

link.reason: Both are Corso's claim in The Day After Roswell that crash materials were recovered and reverse engineered.
link.difference: Speaks generally of crash retrieval programs and puts the work at the Pentagon, without naming Roswell, Hillenkoetter or Bell Labs.

candidates.title: Life magazine withholds the Zapruder film under C.D. Jackson
candidates.quote: Life acquired the Zapruder film, the clearest footage of the assassination, but instead of releasing it in full, they only published black and white stills with certain key frames missing.

link.reason: Both tell of Life magazine under C.D. Jackson putting out the Zapruder film with key frames missing.
link.difference: Adds that only black and white stills were published rather than the full film, and runs the withholding into the 1970s.

candidates.title: 1952 CIA memo on the dangers of flying saucers
candidates.quote: "The flying saucer situation contains two elements of danger, which in a situation of international tension have national security implications. These are psychological and air vulnerability."

link.reason: Both tell of the 1952 CIA memo calling the flying saucer situation a national security matter.
link.difference: Quotes the memo's two dangers, psychological and air vulnerability, and credits it to Walter B. Smith.

candidates.title: Smith's memo to the PSB on 1,500 UFO reports
candidates.quote: Another document, this time from Smith to the director of the Psychological Strategy Board, notes that over 1,500 UFO reports had been logged.
documents: CIA memo to the director of the Psychological Strategy Board

link.reason: Smith's 1952 memo to the director of the Psychological Strategy Board noting 1,500 reports is a separate document from the national security memo and from his 1953 psychological warfare letter.

candidates.title: Herald Tribune 'Conquest of Gravity' series and Gordon Gray's UNC gravity institute
candidates.quote: Anel Talbert wrote an article for the New York Herald Tribune in November of 1955 while Gray was president of the University of North [music] Carolina.
documents: Conquest of gravity aim of top scientists in United States (New York Herald Tribune)

link.reason: Both tell of Talbert's 1950s newspaper series on aerospace interest in anti-gravity.
link.difference: Names the New York Herald Tribune and November 1955 as the paper and date, and ties the series to Gordon Gray as UNC president.

candidates.title: 1956 Chapel Hill gravity conference
candidates.quote: In 1956, this Institute of Field Physics at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, holds what's known as the Chapel Hill Conference, convening all of the world's top theoretical physicists [music] to discuss gravity.

link.reason: Both tell of the famous Chapel Hill gravity conference at UNC.
link.difference: Dates it to 1956 and says the Institute of Field Physics held it, bringing together the world's top theoretical physicists.

candidates.title: Bahnson funds T. Townsend Brown's gravity experiments
candidates.quote: The head of the Institute of Field Physics, Agnu Bonsson, is also funding mid-century inventor Thomas Townsen Brown, who is claiming to get successful positive results on gravity manipulation experiments.

link.reason: Both tell of Agnew Bahnson funding Townsend Brown's gravity experiments.
link.difference: Names Bahnson as head of the Institute of Field Physics and says Brown claimed positive results.

candidates.quote: Gray was also named as one of the advisers on the top secret research and development organization established by Truman as it appears in the leaked Majestic [music] 12 documentation.

link.reason: Gordon Gray being named in the MJ-12 documents is a different story from Menzel being named in them and from the general release of the MJ-12 documents.

candidates.title: Bissell named by Malmgren as the man who briefed him on otherworldly technology

candidates.title: Malmgren clip: 'there are things you need to know'
candidates.quote: Said there are things you need to know.

link.reason: Malmgren's own clip of Bissell telling him there were things he needed to know is part of the same briefing story.

candidates.quote: In 1955, Kissinger was invited to direct a Council on Foreign Relations study group on nuclear war and foreign policy.

link.reason: Kissinger directing the 1955 CFR nuclear weapons study group is not in the corpus; the nearest, Kissinger's Psychological Strategy Board consulting, is a different program.

candidates.title: Rockefeller's panel meets at Quantico
candidates.quote: The group first met at Quantico, Virginia to draft reports for Eisenhower.

link.reason: Rockefeller's panel meeting at Quantico in 1955 to draft reports for Eisenhower matches no story below.

candidates.title: Bluegill Triple Prime detonation downs a UFO
candidates.place_text: Pacific; Albuquerque Operations Office, New Mexico

candidates.title: Malmgren says Gise reverse-engineered recovered craft

link.reason: A rumour that Bissell came back to the CIA the Monday after leaving in 1961. None of the Bissell stories (Area 51, the Malmgren briefings) covers this.

candidates.title: Grusch suggests Dick Cheney was a UFO program gatekeeper
candidates.quote: Modern UFO whistleblower David Grush has suggested that someone like former vice president Dick Cheney was a gatekeeper of the UFO program.
